SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 42.733142, -84.553837 (Approximated from CITY_STATE)

Report Description
****WEB REPORT**** UPON ARRIVAL TO AN FAA FACILITY (LAN VOR), LOCATED IN A RURAL AREA APPROXIMATELY 7 MILES FROM THE AIRPORT, FAA TECHNICIANS DISCOVERED THAT THERE WAS A RELEASE FROM THE FUEL SYSTEM THAT SUPPORTS A BACKUP EMERGENCY GENERATOR AT THE SITE. THE INCIDENT WAS DISCOVERED ON MONDAY, AUGUST 13TH, AND WOULD HAVE OCCURRED SOMETIME BETWEEN THURSDAY, AUGUST 9 AND MONDAY, AUGUST 13TH. IT IS ESTIMATED THAT APPROXIMATELY 100 GALLONS OF #2 DIESEL FUEL WAS LOST FROM THE SYSTEM. SOME OF THE MATERIAL WAS CONTAINED WITHIN THE BUILDING, AND SOME IS BELIEVED TO HAVE BEEN RELEASED TO THE SURROUNDING OUTDOOR AREA BY SEEPING THROUGH THE DOORWAY.

properties.summary: Incident Type: FIXED - NRC Report ID: 986150 - Medium Affected: WATER - Suspected Responsible Party: CENTRAL VERMONT PUBLIC SERVICE CORP.
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 986150
Incident Time: 2011-08-16 03:17:00
Nearest City: Brattleboro, VT
Incident Type: FIXED
Material: OIL, MISC: MINERAL
Medium Affected: WATER
Suspected Responsible Party: CENTRAL VERMONT PUBLIC SERVICE CORP.
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 20 gallons
A LARGE OAK TREE ON WILLIAMS ST. IN DOWNTOWN BRATTLEBORO, VT FELL DURING HEAVY RAIN LATE ON 15 AUG 11. THE TREE DAMAGED ADJACENT OVERHEAD LINES AND BROKE A UTILITY POLE WITH A 25 KVA TRANSFORMER ATTACHED TO IT. APPROXIMATELY 25 GALLONS OF MINERAL OIL SPILLED ONTO PAVEMENT AND THE ROAD SHOULDER. DUE TO RUNOFF FROM THE HEAVY RAIN, SOME OF THE OIL ENTERED INTO TWO CATCH BASINS ADJACENT TO THE SPILL SITE. THE CATCH BASINS APPEAR TO DISCHARGE INTO THE NEARBY WHETSTONE BROOK. THE MINERAL OIL FIELD TESTED AS NON-PCB. ENPRO, A SPILL RESPONSE CONTRACTOR, RESPONDED OVERNIGHT AND REMOVED 13, 55-GAL. DRUMS OF MATERIAL. THE SPILL MATERIAL INCLUDED SOIL, SPEEDY DRY, VEGETATION, DEBRIS AND WATER EXTRACTED FROM THE AFFECTED CATCH BASINS. AFTER THE CLEANUP THERE WERE NO VISIBLE SHEENS IN THE CATCH BASINS NOR IN WHETSTONE BROOK. CENTRAL VERMONT PUBLIC SERVICE TRANSPORTED THE DRUMS AS VT02 WASTES TO ITS BRATTLEBORO SERVICE CENTER AND THEY ARE SCHEDULED FOR TRANSPORT TO THE CVPS TSDF IN RUTLAND, VT.

THE TREE DAMAGED ADJACENT OVERHEAD LINES AND BROKE A UTILITY POLE WITH A 25 KVA TRANSFORMER ATTACHED TO IT. APPROXIMATELY 25 GALLONS OF MINERAL OIL SPILLED ONTO PAVEMENT AND THE ROAD SHOULDER. DUE TO RUNOFF FROM THE HEAVY RAIN, SOME OF THE OIL ENTERED INTO TWO CATCH BASINS ADJACENT TO THE SPILL SITE. THE CATCH BASINS APPEAR TO DISCHARGE INTO THE NEARBY WHETSTONE BROOK. THE MINERAL OIL FIELD TESTED AS NON-PCB. ENPRO, A SPILL RESPONSE CONTRACTOR, RESPONDED OVERNIGHT AND REMOVED 13, 55-GAL. DRUMS OF MATERIAL. THE SPILL MATERIAL INCLUDED SOIL, SPEEDY DRY, VEGETATION, DEBRIS AND WATER EXTRACTED FROM THE AFFECTED CATCH BASINS. AFTER THE CLEANUP THERE WERE NO VISIBLE SHEENS IN THE CATCH BASINS NOR IN WHETSTONE BROOK. CENTRAL VERMONT PUBLIC SERVICE TRANSPORTED THE DRUMS AS VT02 WASTES TO ITS BRATTLEBORO SERVICE CENTER AND THEY ARE SCHEDULED FOR TRANSPORT TO THE CVPS TSDF IN RUTLAND, VT.

properties.title: NRC Report: Oil, Fuel: No. 2 near West Burke, VT
properties.summary: Incident Type: MOBILE - NRC Report ID: 958355 - Medium Affected: SOIL - Suspected Responsible Party: FRED'S PLUMBING & HEATING INC
properties.content:
NRC Report ID: 958355
Incident Time: 2010-09-29 19:25:00
Nearest City: West Burke, VT
Incident Type: MOBILE
Material: OIL, FUEL: NO. 2
Medium Affected: SOIL
Suspected Responsible Party: FRED'S PLUMBING & HEATING INC
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Spill Volume: 20 gallons
ONE OF OUR #2 FUEL OIL DELIVERY DRIVERS NEGOTIATING AN OBSTACLE IN A CUSTOMER'S DRIVEWAY GOT TOO CLOSE TO THE EDGE OF THE SHOULDER WITH A TRUCK WITH ABOUT 2500 GALLONS ONBOARD WENT DOWN OVER AN APPROXIMATE 5 FT EMBANKMENT TIPPING UP ON TO THE RIGHT (PASSENGER) SIDE. THE OPERATOR, WHO WAS NOT INJURED, REPORTED THE INCIDENT TO DISPATCH, THEN FREED HIMSELF FROM HIS SEATBELT AND CLIMBED OUT OF THE TRUCK. HE ASSESSED THE SITUATION AND FOUND THAT THE FRONT MANWAY COVER WAS CLOSED, BUT LEAKING #2 FUEL OIL. THE MIDDLE AND REAR COMPARTMENTS WERE NOT LEAKING #2 FUEL OIL. THE DRIVER PUT A 5 GALLON PAIL UNDER THE LEAK AS WELL AS OIL ABSORBENT PADS ON THE GROUND. THERE WAS EVIDENCE OF SOME #2 FUEL OIL THAT HAD SPRAYED ON NEARBY VEGETATION. THERE WERE NO WATERWAYS NEARBY. WHEN OTHER COMPANY EMPLOYEES ARRIVED ON SCENE, THEY ALSO PUT DOWN OIL ABSORBENT PADS. THE EAST BURKE FIRE BRIGADE RESPONDED TO THE CALL AND PLACED LOCKING CLAMPS ON THE MANWAYS TO ENSURE THEY REMAINED CLOSED. EMERGENCY CREWS REMAINED ONSITE UNTIL AFTER THE TRUCK WAS RIGHTED AND TOWED FROM THE SCENE. AN ENVIRONMENTAL RESPONSE PERSON WAS CALLED ONSITE TO LEAD AND ASSESS THE CLEANUP EFFORT. APPROXIMATELY 10 CUBIC YARDS OF SOIL AND VEGETATION WAS EXCAVATED AND PLACED ON AND COVERED WITH PLASTIC SHEETING. SOIL SAMPLES WERE TAKEN.
